frame:
IDENTITY FIRST — and the identity problem is not damage, it is AGENCY and COLLISION.

Three theses drive everything below.

(1) THE FELT DEFECT IS "MY TURN IS EMPTY", NOT "I DEAL NO DAMAGE." The ledger's rank-1 measurement is the right one: leyline/White has 2 Action-costing talents in 25 and leyline/Blue has 5 (three of which are illusions), against deity trees running 5-8 of 9 and heroic/Warrior at 13 of 25. A White player Draws Mana and then has two Actions their sheet gives them nothing to spend on. Adding a damage talent buys exactly one Action-costing play; buying agency buys three or four, and buys them on-identity. Every proposal here is judged first on whether it changes what the player DOES on their own turn.

(2) WHERE THE PROSE AND THE TALENTS DISAGREE, I FIX WHICHEVER ONE IS NOT LOAD-BEARING. Blue's and White's intent files are correct and delivered — Blue implements Foresight, Calculation and Illusion (it is the only tree in 365 that CREATES illusions); White implements Coordination, Bulwark and Accord, and its Draw Mana rider is the only refuel in the game that is itself an effect. Their prose forecloses damage in one sentence each ("They rarely meet force with force"; "A White mage rarely wins alone") and the talents obey. That prose stays. Sovereignty's prose promises a Decree ZONE that exists in no talent and never has, and its nine talents are two clauses wearing nine names — there the TALENTS are the problem and the promise is the better artefact. Blue's "plot-die capstone identity" line, by contrast, lives in a section whose own header says "reference, not law", is handed to White in the same breath, and is fully implemented by heroic/Agent — there the PROMISE is the problem and I recommend deleting it rather than building it.

(3) THE OVERLAP FIX IS SHARPENING, NOT NERFING — AND ONE OF THE HEADLINE OVERLAPS IS NOT REAL. "Blue and Scholar do the same thing" is false on the evidence and true in the gut, and the gap between those two facts is the whole review. Cosine 0.794 puts Blue<->Scholar at rank 11 of 210, below Black<->Red (0.920), Red<->Envoy (0.877) and Blue<->Red (0.869). Function by function they share nearly nothing: Blue 5 impose-disadvantage / 2 illusion / 4 social / 0 heal against Scholar 1 / 0 / 1 / 2. What they share is an ABSENCE — neither deals damage, both are cerebral, both are Reaction-and-downtime shaped — and an absence cannot be fixed by giving both of them the same new thing. It is fixed by giving each a PRESENCE nobody else has: for Blue, the only stacking numeric penalty in the game; for White, the only ally-buff zone outside the deity atlas; for Scholar (out of remit, named for completeness) nothing, because fabrials and sheet-rewriting already are unique.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE LEDGER I MADE BY READING THE TEXT, because it changes proposal 4 and it is falsifiable: the rank-2 target-count census lists leyline/Green at ZERO multi-enemy damage. That is wrong. leyline/Green's **Thorn Field** (Territory, Passive, no cost, depth 2, earliest L3) reads "Your difficult terrain deals half [Tier][Die] keen damage to characters that enter or start their turn in it", and Green's Attunement Key creates that terrain FREE on every Draw Mana. That is a repeatable, cost-free, multi-enemy damage engine from level 3 — better sustain than anything in the heroic atlas. It was missed because it carries no authored roll formula and delivers damage through a zone rather than through an activation, which is precisely the failure mode the brief warned the census had. The AoE finding survives (13 trees at zero, not 14; the heroic atlas still has one talent, at L6) but Green must come off the list, and Black's Spoils of Isolation must come off the "built backwards" list too: an area attack that scales with how SPREAD OUT the enemies are is exactly correct for the tree whose entire identity is isolation. It is the one AoE in the game built the right way round for its own colour.

proposals.title: WHITE: unjam the Reaction slot and buy the freed budget back as on-turn formation plays
proposals.surface: DATA (data/leyline.json prose + data/authored/leyline-white.json + pack rebuild) plus ONE engine primitive for the buff zone — check ENGINE_INDEX.md first, Green's difficult-terrain placement and Fate's Ordained Ground both already place scene-duration areas and one of them is probably reusable.
proposals.change:
White should uniquely own THE FORMATION: the shape allies stand in, the fortune they share, and the fact that damage aimed at them is permanently smaller. Nobody else in 365 does free, permanent, untriggered, multi-target damage reduction; nobody else manufactures plot dice for other people at scale; nobody else has the anti-Influence package. Three concrete changes.
(a) COLLAPSE THE DUPLICATE TRIGGER. Interposing Shield ('an ally within 10 feet takes damage'), Retributive Guard ('an ally adjacent to you takes damage from an enemy') and Shared Burden ('an ally adjacent to you takes damage') are three Reactions on one event competing for one slot per round. Keep Retributive Guard as the Reaction — it is the one with a payload and White's only damage line. Convert Interposing Shield to a Special riding your Move: 'When you Move, you may move up to 10 feet toward an ally; the next damage they take before the start of your next turn is reduced by half [Tier][Die].' This makes it pre-emptive, puts it on White's own turn, and fixes ledger 15 in the same token (it currently reads half [Die], mitigating ~2.0 at Tier 2 where its two free Passive siblings mitigate ~4.5). Convert Shared Burden to a Passive with a once-per-round internal limiter — its 2 Investiture is already the throttle — and DELETE the 'Strength 3+' clause from its rankGate, which is an attribute gate mis-dated by the skill-rank cap (ledger 20).
(b) ADD A 1-ACTION FORMATION PLACEMENT at depth 0-1. Declare a line or 10-ft area within Attunement Range for the scene (cap: one active). Allies inside it gain the Guardian Stance +1 Deflect whether or not they are adjacent to you, and the first ally to test from inside it each round raises the stakes. This is White's answer to being the only leyline tree with terrain_zone 0, and it is a BUFF zone — no damage, no hazard, no trap — so it does not touch Green's difficult terrain, Destruction's dangerous terrain, or Fate's Ordained Ground (which is ally-anchored and carries a Reactive-Strike grant).
(c) ADD A 2-ACTION OPPORTUNITY SINK at depth 2-3. Spend an Opportunity and 1 Investiture: every ally in Attunement Range chooses one of {Move half Speed without provoking, Aid at no focus cost, remove one condition}. The leyline guide assigns Opportunity to White ('unity generates shared fortune') and White's four plot-die talents already MANUFACTURE Opportunities for other people — Guiding Signal, Concordant Presence, Unity of Purpose and Pillar of Order all push raise-the-stakes onto allies. The loop currently has two sinks (Mending Aura, Collective Resolve) and both are Specials. This is the Action-costing sink it has been building toward.
Net effect: White goes from 2 Action-costing talents in 25 to 4, from 7 Reactions on 5 trigger classes to 6 on 5, and from zero map presence to one buff zone.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 1 in its acute case (White 2/25 agency), ledger 15 (Interposing Shield's half [Die] token), ledger 20 (Shared Burden's Strength 3+ mis-gate). Answers designer question 2 for the specific PC who triggered this review.
proposals.cost: White becomes the strongest support tree in the leyline atlas by a distance, pressing on leyline/Green (buff 3 / healing 5) and heroic/Leader (buff 4 / social 5). Green keeps deep healing and Injury removal; Leader keeps the command die and social leverage; neither loses anything, but the designer should expect the White player to feel like the party's centre. The buff zone is new engine surface unless an existing zone primitive is reused — if it is new, every zone-reading handler needs a regression case. RETEST: the Reaction-slot behaviour on the three collapsed talents, every Draw Mana rider (Beacon of Stability rides the same Action), and Mending Aura's Opportunity cost, whose source prose still owes the authored file a fix.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on the diagnosis (the 2/25 census is the single most defensible number in the whole review and it is recomputable in one pass). MEDIUM on this exact shape — specifically on whether the buff zone should exist at all rather than White simply getting two more Action-costing Accord plays. What would change my mind: a bench pass showing the White player's Reaction slot is genuinely busy every round and the Draw Mana turn feels like a turn — if so, White's agency deficit is smaller than the census implies and (b) is unnecessary.

proposals.title: BLUE: make the disadvantage channel STACK — the only summing numeric penalty in the game — and move Blue's on-turn agency to level 2
proposals.surface: DATA (five authored rules in data/authored/leyline-blue.json rewritten from the binary advantage channel to the edha-next-test-mod `formula` channel, plus prose) AND ENGINE (a clamp in the fold function; item 49 already makes formula entries SUM by term concatenation, so the summing primitive exists and needs no new work — only the cap does).
proposals.change:
Blue should uniquely own THE ARITHMETIC OF FAILURE and THE ROUND BEFORE THE ROUND: committing to a prediction and being paid for it, illusion as a physical object on the map, and a penalty that adds up when everyone else's cancels out. Four concrete changes.
(a) CONVERT THE FIVE DISADVANTAGE TALENTS TO A SUMMING NUMERIC PENALTY. Pattern Recognition, Intercept, False Premise and Probability Cascade currently write the binary advantage scalar, so per SYSTEM-PRIMER.md they boolean-OR into one another and into every other tree's disadvantage — Blue's signature lever is five talents doing one talent's work, and a single ally imposing disadvantage erases the difference between owning one and owning four. Rewrite them onto `edha-next-test-mod`'s `formula` field, which item 49 already makes SUM: Pattern Recognition -1d4, False Premise -1d4, Intercept -1d6 on the declared action, Probability Cascade -1d6 on each of the next two tests. Leave Absolute Stillness as a true disadvantage — it is a STATE ('creatures you have reduced to 0 Speed'), not a stack.
(b) CAP IT, because the objection is correct. The total numeric penalty from Blue on any one test caps at [Tier]d4 — -1d4 (mean -2.5) through level 5, -2d4 (mean -5) from level 6. Calibration: disadvantage on a d20 is worth about -3.3, so the cap is roughly 'less than one disadvantage at Tier 1, about one and a half at Tier 2'. That is a real but bounded improvement, and — this is the point — it lands on a DIFFERENT CHANNEL from the binary scalar, so a Blue character stacking with an ally who imposes disadvantage now gets both, where today the ally's contribution deletes Blue's.
(c) MOVE READ INTENT FORWARD. It is 1 Action / 1 Investiture at depth 3, earliest L4, and it is the purest expression of Blue's stated fantasy in the tree. Move it to depth 1 (L2) and make it a Special riding Draw Mana — Blue's Key already grants advantage on the next Cognitive test and Read Intent tests Blue vs Cognitive, so the two were built for each other and are eight levels apart.
(d) ADD ONE 1-ACTION 'FORCE A DECLARATION' TALENT at depth 0-1: 1 Action, 1 Investiture, test Blue vs Cognitive; on success the target must declare its next action openly and may not change it. This is the Foresight entry Blue's prose promises and does not have, it is the only compel-a-declaration effect in 365, and it feeds Forewarned and Intercept, which are otherwise the player guessing.
(e) DO NOT BUILD BLUE PLOT-DIE TALENTS. See ledger 11 and the argument in my Sovereignty/Blue positions — the promise is in the self-deprecated section, heroic/Agent owns the plot die completely (6 talents, the only rerolls in 365), and Blue's binding intent file never mentions it. Recommend DELETING the sentence from the guide instead, and deleting White's duplicate claim to the same key mechanic in the same section.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 1 (the Blue half — 5/25 to 7/25 Action-costing, and the two best new plays are at L1-2 rather than L6), ledger 11 (settles it as a deliberate NO, with the guide line deleted rather than left lying), ledger 14 partially (it establishes the summing channel as a supported, capped, talent-facing mechanic rather than an unproven adversary-only primitive). Directly answers the designer's Blue<->Scholar question.
proposals.cost: Blue becomes the game's best debuffer, which presses on leyline/Black (debuff 4) and heroic/Leader (debuff 3). Black keeps Weakened, the isolation lock and Hollow Command's whole-turn denial; Leader keeps the command die. The real risk is the one the completeness critic named: the formula channel is used today by ONE adversary ability (Probability Net) and by zero talents, so this is its first real load. RETEST: edhaNextModFoldMode against mixed binary+formula entries; Probability Net; and every talent in any tree that reads advantage state. Pin a regression case in tests/ per iron rule 4.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the identity is right — a stacking penalty is unique in 365 and it is exactly what 'bending probability' should mean mechanically. MEDIUM on the magnitudes. What would change my mind: bench arithmetic showing -2d4 on top of an ally's disadvantage makes Tier-2 enemies fail routinely; if so drop the per-source values to -1d4 flat and cap at -1d4+[Tier].

proposals.title: SOVEREIGNTY: build the Decree as a real dual-polarity zone at the top of the tree, and make both entries land on turn one
proposals.surface: DATA (data/domain.json prose + data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json + pack rebuild) plus a zone/aura primitive if none is reusable. Do NOT start this until ledger 7 (the two contradictory temporary-HP writers) is settled, because Exalt's temp HP becomes load-bearing under (b).
proposals.change:
Sovereignty should uniquely own THE DUAL-POLARITY AURA: one declared area that elevates allies and diminishes enemies at the same time. No other tree in 365 has an aura that does opposite things to the two sides, and that is a genuinely distinctive space that the intent prose already claims in bold and the deity guide repeats without a disclaimer. Today all nine talents are single-target, the word Decree appears only inside the talent name 'Decree of Ruin', and the nine are assembled from two clauses ('damage die size increases by one step (maximum d12)' in four; 'decreases by one step (minimum d4)' in four plus the capstone). Four changes.
(a) BUILD DECREE WHERE THE REDUNDANCY ALREADY IS. Do not rewrite all nine. Convert the two talents that are pure repetition — Sovereign's Balance (depth 2) and the Sovereignty capstone (depth 3) — into Decree zones: a [Size]-radius area at a point in Attunement Range, scene duration, cap ONE active Decree; allies inside are Exalted (+1 die step), enemies inside Censured (-1 die step); the capstone makes it +/-2 and keeps the enemy reaction-lock clause. This turns the tree's two most redundant nodes into the two that deliver the promise, and it fixes the deity guide's own named pitfall ('synthesis nodes that just repeat tier-2').
(b) MAKE BOTH ENTRIES LAND ON TURN ONE (deity revision Principle 1). One die step is +/-1.0 average per die and is worth exactly ZERO against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus — it is below the threshold at which a person at a table notices anything happened. Give each entry a second, perceptible rider inside the tree's own vocabulary: Censure also makes the target's damage die size unable to be INCREASED by any effect while Censured (a real, unique counter to Exalt-likes, Knowledge's Insight multiplier and Power's riders); Exalt folds in the temporary HP that Sovereign's Favor currently sells as a separate purchase.
(c) RE-SPEND SOVEREIGN'S FAVOR. With its temp HP folded into Exalt, repurpose it as the tree's Special — 'you may apply Exalt as a Special riding your Draw Mana, or riding the Exalted ally's Strike'. That gives the deity atlas its first Special (see proposal 7) in the tree that most needs the action relief.
(d) PRINT THE COLOUR ON THE CARD. Every Sovereignty card says '[Tier][Die]' and names no colour. In fact data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json contains exactly one @skills.white.rank, in handler SovFavorThp00000, formula (@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2) — Sovereign's Favor's temp HP is a [Tier][Die on White], and that is the ONLY thing the tree's White 3+ gate buys. Print it. A player choosing a third rank of Black over a third of White is currently choosing blind.
IF THE DESIGNER REJECTS THE ZONE: then take the other exit explicitly and DELETE the Decree promise from data/path-descriptions.json and from the deity guide's Part 4. What must not happen is the prose continuing to promise a radius the tree does not have — that is the first thing a player reads when choosing a god.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 4 in full (the absent signature resource, the two-clause construction, and the sub-perceptual payload), the Sovereignty half of the deity-gate/toll-booth finding, and one of the ten deity Special zeroes.
proposals.cost: A zone version of Censure hits several enemies at once in a tree that today hits one, which is a real power jump — hence the ONE-active cap and holding the payload at +/-1 outside the capstone, so the change buys breadth rather than depth. Sovereignty's elevate half already overlaps deity/Knowledge's The Pack; the zone sharpens the difference (Knowledge multiplies dice on one MARKED TARGET, Sovereignty steps dice inside a PLACE) rather than deepening it. RETEST: the whole die-size sealed loop (4 producers / 7 consumers), Sovereign's Favor's temp HP under whichever writer wins ledger 7, and the capstone's reaction-lock.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on the diagnosis — Decree's absence is checkable in one grep and the two-clause construction is countable. MEDIUM on this being the right remedy: the honest alternative is that Verdannis is simply a single-target arbiter and the prose oversold him, in which case (b) and (d) still stand alone and are worth doing on their own.

proposals.title: GREEN: the cluster engine has jaws, but they are blunt and they bite the party — sharpen them, and correct the AoE census
proposals.surface: DATA (data/leyline.json prose + data/authored/leyline-green.json + pack rebuild). Almost certainly no engine work: Thorn Field is already wired (events=1) and the terrain-tick primitive exists.
proposals.change:
FIRST, THE CORRECTION. The ledger's rank-2 census lists leyline/Green at zero multi-enemy damage. It is wrong. **Thorn Field** (Territory, Passive, NO cost, NO action, depth 2, earliest L3) reads 'Your difficult terrain deals half [Tier][Die] keen damage to characters that enter or start their turn in it', and Green's Attunement Key creates difficult terrain FREE on every Draw Mana. That is a free, repeatable, multi-enemy damage engine available from level 3 with better sustain than anything in the heroic atlas. It was missed because it carries no authored roll formula and delivers damage through a zone rather than an activation — exactly the class of miss the brief warned about. Green comes off the zero list; the finding stands at 13 trees, not 14. Take leyline/Black's Spoils of Isolation off the 'built backwards' list too: an area attack that scales with how spread out the enemies are is CORRECT for the only tree whose identity is isolation, and it is the one AoE in the game built the right way round for its own colour.
SECOND, THE ACTUAL GREEN DEFECT. The guide says 'Green's cluster engine mirrors Black's isolation engine' — but Black's engine has a payload chain (Key applies Weakened -> Sapping Hex -> Spoils of Isolation -> the vital line) while Green's payoff for a successful clump is Apex Predator, which at depth 3 / L6 grants ONE BINARY ADVANTAGE for having three or more enemies in your terrain. That is the strongest cluster condition in the game paying out in the game's least stackable currency. Two changes: (i) raise Thorn Field's payload from 'half [Tier][Die]' to '[Tier][Die]' and scope it to ENEMIES rather than 'characters' — friendly fire on terrain your own Key creates for free every refuel is a tax the party pays for Green existing, and it is the reason a Green player learns not to use their own Attunement rider; (ii) rebuild Apex Predator's payout as a scaling numeric or damage effect keyed to the count of clustered enemies rather than a binary advantage.
proposals.resolves: Corrects ledger 2's census (and, with it, any 'the leyline atlas cannot answer a group' claim). Sharpens Green<->Black, which is the guide's own stated mirror pair. Removes the anti-synergy where Green's free Key damages allies.
proposals.cost: Green's damage_direct rises from 2 toward 3, pressing on leyline/Red's area identity — keep the payload TERRAIN-GATED so it is never a targeted nuke and Red keeps sole ownership of aimed area damage (Flame Surge, Arc Flash, Chain Detonation). Enemies-only terrain damage is a genuine buff to a tree already scoring healing 5; if that is too much, take (ii) alone and leave Thorn Field's number where it is. RETEST: the terrain-tick handler against allies standing in Green terrain, and Apex Predator's trigger count.
proposals.confidence: HIGH — Thorn Field's text is verbatim in the dossier and the census miss is reproducible. The remedy is MEDIUM-HIGH; (i) and (ii) are independent and either can be taken alone.

proposals.title: DEITY: raise the signature-resource cap from 'up to your tier' to 'up to 1 + your tier'
proposals.surface: DATA — one clause per talent across six trees in data/domain.json plus the matching authored descriptions, plus pack rebuild. No engine work if the caps are read from the talent text; if any cap is hard-coded in a handler, that handler changes too.
proposals.change: Six deity trees cap their signature resource at 'up to your tier', which is ONE for the whole of levels 1-5 — the exact span this campaign occupies. The consequences are not cosmetic: deity/Civilization's Trade Routes ('choose two of your active Foundations', depth 1, dated L2) is UNCASTABLE before level 6; deity/Chaos's Cascade Collapse and Unravel Everything both detonate 'all your Omens' and are therefore single-target through L5; Spreading Omen ('one additional enemy, subject to your Omen cap') is dominated by its own entry; deity/Destruction's Cascading Failure needs 'two or more Charges' it cannot have; deity/Order's Lawkeeper's Eye and Final Decree run off a single Edict. Change the cap wording to '1 + your tier' (2 at Tier 1, 3 at Tier 2) in Chaos/Entropy Strike, Order/Edict, Order/Covenant, Civilization/Lay Foundation, Destruction/Set Charge, Fate/Ordained Ground, Fate/Snare and Death/Risen Servant. Separately, deity/Civilization's Forge Construct reads 'You may sustain one active Construct' — a flat 1 that never scales with tier, uniquely among the ten sustain clauses; either bring it onto the same ladder or leave it deliberately flat, but decide rather than leaving it as an unexplained outlier.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 12 in full. Unlocks one uncastable talent and at least four strictly-dominated ones at the levels the campaign is actually at.
proposals.cost: Every deity tree gets materially stronger at levels 1-5, widening the deity<->leyline gap the primer explicitly flags as the thing to watch ('9 deity talents outclassing 25 leyline talents in TOTAL would be' the bug). The counter-argument is real: the cap is part of what makes level 6 a step change, and deity/Knowledge — whose Insight cap is a flat 5 — is the strongest damage tree in the game, which is some evidence that uncapped-at-tier is where the power is. RETEST: every sealed-loop handler that reads a cap (Omen, Charge, Edict, Covenant, Ordained Ground, Snare, Harvested Remain, Risen Servant).
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH that something must change here — an uncastable depth-1 talent is not defensible on any reading. MEDIUM on '1 + tier' as the number; a flat 2 at all tiers is the conservative alternative and unblocks everything named above.

proposals.title: HYGIENE BUNDLE: six one-line fixes, each of which is a live lie on a card or in a guide
proposals.surface: DATA only, all six. Two need a pack rebuild (the Death connections and Frightened, because they change talent documents); the guide and typo fixes do not.
proposals.change:
(a) deity/Death's two iron-rule-7 prose-vs-connections divergences, live on main and passing all gates because validateConnections only checks that a name resolves: Raise Dead's card says 'Necrotic Cascade or Speak with the Fallen' while connections is ['Necrotic Cascade','Risen Servant'] — Foundry demands Risen Servant, which the card never names, and ignores Speak with the Fallen, which it does. Necrotic Cascade's card says 'Consuming Decay' while connections is ['Consuming Decay','Death Ward'] — Death Ward is silently ANDed on. Align both, in whichever direction the designer intends; the card and the connections must name the same parents.
(b) The Frightened condition is required by deity/Power's Kneel (advantage rider) and Absolute Authority (target requirement) and is produced by NO talent in 365. Identity-first answer: do not delete the word — deity/Power is the CONQUEROR, and Frightened is the one condition a conqueror should manufacture. Add production to Kneel's failure clause (a target that resists Kneel becomes Frightened) and the dead clauses come alive without touching anything else.
(c) leyline/Blue's Counterspell cost field reads '2 Focus; 1 Investiure' at data/leyline.json:840. One character. It silently removes Blue from every regex census (Blue is 16 Investiture-costers, not 15) and has already caused one analyst to 'correct' a correct figure back to the wrong one.
(d) deity/Chaos's capstone Unravel Everything is the only one of ten deity capstones with no 'once per scene' limiter — at 3 Investiture it repeats every turn the player can pay. Nine trees pay the tax; make it ten, or state that Chaos is deliberately exempt.
(e) The leyline design guide states Black's Draw Mana rider as 'no ally within 10 ft'. Every shipped talent uses 5 ft — the Black Attunement Key, Sapping Hex, and deity/Chaos's Isolated definition. The guide is stale and will mis-author the next Black or Power talent written from it.
(f) leyline/White's Mending Aura: the authored text costs 'an Opportunity AND 1 Investiture', the source prose costs Opportunity only. The authored text wins in Foundry; the source prose owes the fix. This is the single material authored-divergence in all 365.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 9, 5, 18, 16, 19, and the Mending Aura half of 20.
proposals.cost: Essentially nil. (a) and (b) need a pack rebuild and therefore Ben's deploy step; the rest are repo-side. Nothing gets weaker. The only judgment inside the bundle is (b)'s direction — add a Frightened producer versus delete the word — and (d)'s exemption question.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on all six. Each is checkable in a single grep against the file named.

proposals.title: DEITY: give the atlas its missing Specials by converting the riders that already ride something else
proposals.surface: DATA (action-type field plus prose in data/domain.json and the authored overlay) + pack rebuild. No engine work — the action type is a document field.
proposals.change: Zero Specials exist across all ninety deity talents, against a written 15-20% target that the leyline atlas hit (27 of 125 = 22%) after a revision pass explicitly aimed at the same defect. The deity guide's own Principle 10 says a talent that applies an upgrade rider during another talent's activation IS a Free Action, not an Action — so the conversion is the guide correcting itself, not a power grant. Convert ONLY talents that already ride another action, one or two per tree: deity/Sovereignty's Sovereign's Favor (rides Exalt — see proposal 3c), deity/Order's Sealed Edict (rides Edict placement), deity/Death's Withering Touch (a rider on a melee weapon attack — textbook Special), deity/Civilization's Tempered Edge (rides the Construct's attack), deity/Knowledge's Accumulate (rides your turn), deity/Life's Prognosis (rides a Diagnosed creature taking damage), deity/Chaos's Void Sense (rides an Omen-bearer taking damage). Do NOT convert standalone effects — that is where the objection bites.
proposals.cost: The defence advocate's objection is correct and survives: making deity effects cheaper in actions widens exactly the deity-vs-leyline action-efficiency gap the primer flags, and deity trees already run 5-8 Action-costing talents in 9 against leyline's 4-6 in 25. That is precisely why the scope here is 'riders only'. If the designer wants deity Specials broadly, do proposals 1 and 2 (leyline agency) FIRST so the comparison does not get worse before it gets better. RETEST: nothing mechanical — but every converted talent's action-economy assumption in the checklist needs re-walking at the bench.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on the conversion being correct per the guide. LOW-MEDIUM on it being URGENT — this is a conformance gap that a player is unlikely to feel, unlike proposals 1-4.

proposals.title: DEITY GATES: give the four near-dead gate colours a job, or drop them
proposals.surface: DATA (card prose + authored formulas) + pack rebuild.
proposals.change: Correcting the record first, because the published 'four of five toll booths are WHITE' claim is 1-for-4 wrong: counting BOTH channels in data/authored/deity-*.json (@skills.<colour>.rank AND the color/rangeColor targeting fields) leaves exactly ONE pure toll booth — deity/Fate's White 2+, with zero references of either kind — and three near-dead gates: Sovereignty/White (1 reference), Destruction/Blue (1), Life/Blue (1). Three of those four are not White. Two changes. (a) For Fate, give White the job the deity guide already assigns it: 'Ordained Ground (White-flavored, ally-anchored)'. Size Ordained Ground's +1-to-all-defenses and Bulwark Ground's temporary HP on White rank rather than leaving them tierless, and the gate stops being a toll. (b) For the other three plus Sovereignty, PRINT THE COLOUR on the card: every deity card today reads '[Tier][Die]' and names no colour, so a player deciding between a third rank of Black and a third of White cannot see which one their tree uses. That is a card-text fix and it is the whole of the felt problem.
proposals.resolves: The gate-audit / toll-booth family, and the card-blindness that makes it invisible to the player who is paying for it.
proposals.cost: (a) makes deity/Fate's ally-facing half scale where it currently does not, a modest buff to a tree that scores damage_direct 3. (b) costs nothing and breaks nothing. RETEST: Fate's Ordained Ground and Bulwark Ground formulas.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on (b) — it is pure information. MEDIUM on (a); the alternative is simply to drop Fate's White 2+ gate, which is cheaper but discards the guide's own colour split for that tree.

proposals.title: ENGINE: unify the two temporary-HP writers, and rule on which behaviour is canon, BEFORE any temp-HP arithmetic is trusted
proposals.surface: ENGINE (module-src/scripts/engine/28-temporary-hp.js and 51-green-restoration.js, assembled per item 4), plus one authored description in data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json.
proposals.change: Three behaviours are in circulation. 28-temporary-hp.js line 6 documents 'a larger grant replaces a smaller one'; line 13 of the SAME FILE documents 'a new grant OVERWRITES the old, even if smaller'; the code implements the second (edhaWriteTempHp sets the flag unconditionally). 51-green-restoration.js:93's edhaGrantTempHpCross computes wins = inc > (held?.value ?? 0) and keeps the higher. And deity/Sovereignty's Sovereign's Favor card asserts a third position by implication ('This talent's temporary HP does not stack', implying other temp HP does). Fourteen talents across nine trees produce temporary HP. RECOMMENDATION: keep-the-higher, because it is what two of the three surfaces already say, it is what a player expects (an ally helping you should never shrink your shield), and overwrite-even-if-smaller is the only one nobody wrote on a card. Unify both writers on it, delete the contradicting header line, and pin a regression case.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 7. Also invalidates and then repairs every temp-HP-summed-over-rounds figure produced anywhere in this review (Order's Bear Witness, Sovereignty's swing arithmetic) — those numbers should not be quoted again until this lands.
proposals.cost: Keep-the-higher is a net buff wherever two sources currently collide, concentrated in deity/Order (3 producers), Power, Life and Sovereignty (2 each). Scope caveat worth stating plainly: this is an ENGINE question, not a 365-talent question — it is in this list only because proposal 3 makes Sovereignty's Exalt temp HP load-bearing and cannot be costed until it is settled.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the contradiction exists (both files quoted verbatim). MEDIUM-HIGH on keep-the-higher being the right canon.

proposals.title: RED: settle Momentum's Edge at the bench, then reprice it — do not redesign it
proposals.surface: First a BENCH measurement (two minutes: evaluate @movement.walk.rate against a live actor in Foundry), then a one-token DATA edit in data/authored/leyline-red.json.
proposals.change: Momentum's Edge is a free, no-action, depth-2 (L3) Passive whose card reads 'bonus impact damage equal to your Speed' and whose authored handler reads bonusFormula = @movement.walk.rate, with damage.formula null. Three readings are all live and the text supports all three: (a) @movement.walk.rate is a DerivedValueField object and resolves to nothing, so the talent silently does nothing; (b) it resolves to a movement rate in feet, ~+25-30 flat impact, against +1 to +4 for every other damage rider in the game; (c) 'Speed' is a tested SKILL in this system (deity/Destruction's Concussive Yield tests Speed vs. your Red; deity/Fate's Inevitable Snare tests Speed vs. your Green) and every other attribute-reading rider in the corpus means the MODIFIER (Withering Ray '+ Presence', Withering Touch '+ WIL', Snare '+ Awareness'), which would make it +2 to +5. MEASURE FIRST. Then, identity-first: Red's stated identity IS momentum, so a damage rider that pays for charging is exactly right and should not be redesigned away. If it resolves to feet, reprice it — floor(@movement.walk.rate / 10), i.e. +2 to +3 for a 20-30 ft run-up — which preserves the identity and kills the outlier. If it resolves to nothing, the same repricing fixes it.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 6. It is the only place in the whole review where one measurement decides whether leyline/Red is the game's best damage tree at levels 1-5 or a mid-table one, so it also gates any final answer to designer question 1.
proposals.cost: Under reading (b), repricing is a substantial nerf to leyline/Red's real ceiling — but a ceiling nobody knew existed and which no other rider in the game approaches. Under (a) it is a pure buff to a talent currently doing nothing. RETEST: the rider on a live actor at both tiers, and Red's damage census afterwards.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that it must be measured before anything else is said about it. The three-reading framing is the honest epistemic position and it cannot be closed from talent text alone.

proposals.title: HEROIC: give the atlas a level-6 step by repivoting the two dead tier terms — but recognise the ratio cannot be settled inside the fence
proposals.surface: DATA — two formulas in the authored heroic overlay. Two tokens.
proposals.change: Every leyline and deity damage formula is (@tier)d(2 * @skills.<colour>.rank + 2), which goes 1d6 to 2d8 at level 6 — a factor of 2.57 in one step. Every heroic damage formula is flat across the whole L1-10 window, and two of them are flat for a specific, fixable reason: Devastating Blow is (2 + max(@tier - 2, 0))d8 and Wit's End is (4 + max((@tier - 2) * 2, 0))d6, whose tier terms are dead until Tier 3 = level 11, outside this campaign entirely. Repivot both to max(@tier - 1, ...) so they step at Tier 2 / level 6. That gives the heroic atlas ONE discontinuity to sit alongside leyline's, at the same level, for two tokens. STATE THE LIMIT HONESTLY: this does not settle heroic<->leyline parity. Heroic damage rides on a weapon whose dice grow with equipment, and leyline damage is self-contained, so excluding weapon dice 'from both sides' is not symmetric — it subtracts real output from one side of every comparison. Weapons are outside the scope fence. What would settle it is the weapon damage table, and until someone reads it, no heroic-vs-leyline damage RATIO in this review should be quoted as fact. Note also that gate TIMING is already symmetric (heroic 5-7 rank-3 talents per tree, mean 6.0; leyline 5-8, mean 6.4), so the widely-repeated 'leyline is uniquely back-loaded' framing is false and scaling is the only real asymmetry.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 3, to the extent it can be resolved inside the fence.
proposals.cost: Two heroic talents get stronger from level 6. Devastating Blow at 3d8 and Wit's End at 6d6 (Deflect-ignoring) are both meaningful jumps in heroic/Warrior specifically, which already scores damage_direct 4 and holds 13 Action-costing talents. If the answer is that heroic should NOT step, then the right change is the opposite one — delete the dead max() terms entirely so nobody mistakes them for scaling that exists.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the two terms are dead in the campaign's level range (arithmetic, not judgment). LOW-MEDIUM on whether heroic SHOULD step at L6 — that is a designer call about whether magic is meant to outpace martial prowess at Tier 2, and it is the real question behind designer question 2.

proposals.title: SHARED STOCK: do NOT de-duplicate. Reprice the three pricing outliers instead
proposals.surface: DATA (three rankGate / depth fields) + pack rebuild. Explicitly a recommendation to NOT do the larger change.
proposals.change: Roughly 40 talent slots (11%) are duplicate stock — 12 duplicate-name families = 39 slots, 12 byte-identical-text families = 36 slots, and they are not the same twelve; Hardy alone is 7 slots in 7 trees under 3 text variants, so both measures undercount. It is concentrated in heroic (30 of 150 slots) and absent from deity (0 of 90). RECOMMENDATION: leave it. Combat Training gates Devastating Blow; Hardy gates Swift Strikes in Warrior and Unrelenting Salvo in Hunter — they are load-bearing MANAGED PREREQUISITES, and lifting them out severs connections edges. That is squarely iron rule 7 territory in a review that has already found two live connections divergences on main (proposal 6a), and the graph repair costs more than the ~29 slots returned. It is also the least-felt finding in the whole ledger: a player sees the talents in their own tree, and two players would have to lay sheets side by side to notice. DO instead the one thing that IS felt — the pricing inconsistency. Collected ('Increase your Cognitive and Spiritual defenses by 2') is free at depth 0 / L1 in heroic/Envoy, depth 3 / L4 in leyline/Green, and costs a Blue 3+ / LEVEL 6 slot in leyline/Blue, where it is one of only eight talents that tree can take at L6. Either drop Blue's and Green's gates to match Envoy's, or remove Collected from Blue entirely and spend the slot on proposal 2's 'force a declaration' talent. One false positive should also be struck from every published count: 'Shatter Focus' exists in leyline/Red and deity/Chaos with genuinely different mechanics — a name collision, not shared stock — so the widely-quoted '41 slots' figure is unsupported on either measure.
proposals.resolves: Ledger 13, by ruling most of it out of scope and doing the felt remainder.
proposals.cost: Nothing gets weaker; one Blue slot is freed. The cost of NOT doing the larger change is that the heroic atlas keeps feeling less distinct than the leyline one — which is real, but is better fixed by giving heroic paths new identity talents than by deleting shared ones.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that de-duplication is the wrong move (the iron-rule-7 argument is decisive). HIGH on the Collected repricing.

singleFirstChange:
GIVE leyline/WHITE A 1-ACTION, SCENE-DURATION FORMATION PLACEMENT (proposal 1b): declare a line or 10-ft area within Attunement Range, one active at a time; allies inside gain Guardian Stance's +1 Deflect whether or not they are adjacent to you, and the first ally to test from inside it each round raises the stakes.

Why this one, out of everything above. The review exists because two PCs feel like they have nothing to do, and White is the acute case by a wide margin — 2 Action-costing talents in 25, against 5 for Blue, 4-8 in NINE for every deity tree, and 13 for heroic/Warrior. That is the most defensible number in the entire ledger and it is recomputable in one pass. This change takes White from 2 to 3 immediately, and unlike anything else on the list it changes what the White player does on their own turn NEXT SESSION rather than what their sheet says.

It is also the cheapest defensible change of the twelve. It needs no designer ruling on damage; it needs no engine work if an existing zone primitive is reusable (check ENGINE_INDEX.md — Green's difficult-terrain placement and Fate's Ordained Ground both place scene-duration areas); it is a data edit plus a pack rebuild; it nerfs nothing; it breaks no connections edge; and it is pure identity — the intent file's Coordination and Bulwark specialties both describe formations, and White is the only leyline tree with terrain_zone 0 despite its whole prose being about where people stand. It collides with nothing: it is a buff area with no damage, no hazard and no trap, so Green keeps difficult terrain, Destruction keeps dangerous terrain, and Fate keeps Ordained Ground and Snares.

And it is the change most likely to teach us whether the rest of the ledger is right. If the White player comes back and says the turn now feels like a turn, the agency diagnosis is confirmed and proposals 1-2 should be built out in full. If they come back and say it still feels flat, then the diagnosis is wrong, the damage question genuinely re-opens, and I would want to know that before spending an engine change on Blue's summing penalty channel.
argumentOnBlueWhiteDamage:
MY POSITION: NEITHER BLUE NOR WHITE SHOULD GET AN ATTACK TALENT. BOTH SHOULD GET ON-TURN ACTIONS. The two things are being confused, and the confusion is the reason this review was commissioned.

1. THE SYMPTOM IS REAL AND THE PROPOSED CAUSE IS WRONG. What a player at the table experiences is not "I deal zero damage" — a Blue player who Counterspells an enemy's Investiture-fuelled talent has plainly, visibly done something, and a White player whose Shield Wall shaves 4.5 off every attack against two adjacent allies is contributing every round. What they experience is: "I have three Actions on a Slow turn and my twenty-five-talent tree gives me two things to spend them on." That is measured, not inferred: leyline/White 2 of 25 Action-costing talents, leyline/Blue 5 of 25 (three of them illusions), against deity trees at 5-8 of NINE. Adding a damage talent buys ONE Action-costing play. Buying agency buys three or four, and buys them without touching what either tree is FOR.

2. THE PROSE FORECLOSES DAMAGE IN ONE SENTENCE EACH, AND THE TALENTS OBEY. INTENT-leyline-Blue.md: "They rarely meet force with force. A Blue mage prefers to know, to prepare, and to redirect." INTENT-leyline-White.md: "They draw their power from unity rather than self. A White mage rarely wins alone." Both files then name three specialties each, and both trees implement all three — Blue is the only tree in all 365 that CREATES illusions; White owns the only Draw Mana rider that pays the party, the only free permanent multi-target damage reduction, and the only reactive death-denial for someone else. This is the rare case where the prose is right, the talents are right, and only the SHAPE is wrong. The designer's own framing agrees ("That was originally part of the design"). The live question was never whether the absence was intended; it is whether the replacement is FELT, and the answer to that is action density, not damage.

3. ADDING DAMAGE WOULD MAKE THE OVERLAP PROBLEM WORSE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE REMIT. White's single existing damage line — Retributive Guard, punish-the-attacker spirit damage on a Reaction — is already deity/Order's entire identity (an Edict punishes the first forbidden act, for [Tier][Die] + Intellect spirit, plus Disoriented) built with more machinery. Give White a second punishment channel and you have two trees doing Tessavain's job, one of them without his resources. Blue's nearest plausible damage would have to be probability-flavoured or foreknowledge-triggered, which is deity/Fate's ground (Snares, declared triggers) and deity/Chaos's ground (mark-and-detonate). The remit says the fix for overlap is to sharpen both identities. Damage sharpens neither; it is the one addition guaranteed to point both trees at ground someone else already holds.

4. "BLUE AND SCHOLAR DO THE SAME THING" IS FALSE AS STATED AND TRUE AS FELT, AND THAT DISTINCTION SETTLES THE QUESTION. On the numbers it is not close: cosine 0.794 puts Blue<->Scholar at rank 11 of 210 pairs, BELOW Black<->Red (0.920), Red<->Envoy (0.877), Blue<->Red (0.869) and Black<->Envoy (0.867) — pairs nobody has complained about. Function by function they share almost nothing: Blue 5 impose-disadvantage / 3 grant-action / 2 illusion / 4 social / 0 heal, against Scholar 1 / 1 / 0 / 1 / 2. What they actually share is an ABSENCE — no damage, cerebral flavour, Reaction-and-downtime turn shape — and you cannot fix a shared absence by giving both of them the same new thing, which is exactly what "add damage" would be. You fix it by giving each a PRESENCE nobody else has. For Blue that presence is available and cheap: convert its five binary disadvantage talents onto the summing numeric channel (edha-next-test-mod's formula field, which item 49 already makes add) and Blue becomes the only tree in the game whose debuffs STACK — including stacking on top of an ally's disadvantage, which today deletes them. Scholar needs nothing: it already owns fabrials outright (5 of 365 talents, all Scholar) and is the only tree in the game that rewrites its own character sheet.

5. THE ONE CONCESSION, IF THE DESIGNER WANTS DAMAGE ANYWAY. Put it in BLUE, not White, and make it a CONSEQUENCE rather than an attack: damage that fires when a prediction comes true (the character named by Forewarned takes the declared action) or when one of your illusions is destroyed. That stays entirely inside the Foresight and Illusion vocabulary, creates no attack roll, cannot be spammed, and reads as "the world punished them for being predictable" rather than "the tactician learned a spell". White should stay at exactly one damage line — Retributive Guard — because White's whole claim is that it wins through other people, and a White mage who kills things is a worse marshal, not a better one.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND, precisely. (a) A bench pass showing the White player's Reaction slot is genuinely occupied every round and the Draw Mana turn (party heal via the Key, plus Beacon of Stability stripping a condition) reads as a full turn at the table — if so White's agency deficit is smaller than the 2/25 census implies and the damage question honestly re-opens. (b) The Momentum's Edge measurement (proposal 10): if it resolves to feet, leyline/Red is carrying a free +25-30 rider and the intra-leyline damage spread is far wider than anyone has assumed, which changes what "no damage" costs a White or Blue player standing next to a Red one. (c) Anything from the adversary statblocks, which are outside the scope fence — whether a four-PC party with two zero-damage members can actually finish a fight in a reasonable number of rounds is a question about enemy HP, and no amount of reading the 365 talents will answer it. That is the one thing I would want measured before ruling the damage question permanently closed.
argumentOnSovereignty:
SOVEREIGNTY IS THE ATLAS'S WORST TREE AND ITS PROBLEM IS NOT THAT IT DEALS NO DAMAGE — it is that it makes a promise a player reads BEFORE they roll a die, and then delivers two sentences wearing nine names, at a magnitude below the threshold at which a human notices anything happened.

THE THREE DEFECTS, in order of how early a player hits them.
(a) THE PROMISE. INTENT-deity-Sovereignty.md prints in bold: "Signature resource: Decree — a declared law projected within a radius: allies inside are elevated, enemies inside are diminished", and the deity guide repeats it — "Decree zones (declared laws within a radius)", with the gameplay loop "diminish target -> elevate ally -> bring them into Decree" — in a Part 4 that carries NO "reference, not law" disclaimer (unlike the leyline Part 4 that the Blue plot-die claim lives in; that asymmetry is exactly why this drift is real and the Blue one is not). All nine talents target "a creature in Attunement Range" or "a willing ally". A search of the tree for radius, aura, zone or area returns nothing. "Decree" appears only inside the talent name "Decree of Ruin". A player chooses Verdannis because of that paragraph.
(b) THE CONSTRUCTION. Four talents carry "damage die size increases by one step (maximum d12)"; four carry "decreases by one step (minimum d4)"; the capstone carries both at two steps. That is a denser internal redundancy than any cross-tree pair anyone found in this review, and it trips the deity guide's own named pitfall — "synthesis nodes that just repeat tier-2. If the synthesis is tier-2A but a little more, it should be cut."
(c) THE MAGNITUDE. One die step is +/-1.0 average per die. Against the corpus's flat-damage riders — deity/Power's Momentum of Victory, heroic/Agent's Cheap Shot, deity/Knowledge's Pack Share, deity/Life's Vital Diagnosis — it is worth exactly ZERO, because there is no die to step. And the elevate half cannot pay out twice: Investiture of Authority (+1 scene) and the capstone (+2 scene) compete for the same headroom, and on a rank-3 ally already rolling d8 there are only two rungs to the d12 ceiling.

THE DEFENCE IS PARTLY RIGHT AND I AM ADOPTING IT. Two of the objections survive and both change my recommendation rather than defeating it.
First, the tree is not empty. Sovereign's Favor grants [Tier][Die] temporary HP on every Exalt (~3.5 at Tier 1, ~9.0 at Tier 2), unmediated by the die ladder and repeatable from level 2. Expose is a free level-2 Passive that generates Investiture uncapped and converts every enemy miss into an ally's Reactive Strike. Edict of the Fallen buys a scene-long -2 steps plus party temp HP for 2 Actions at level 3. Those are real talents and the "nine axes at zero, lowest axis sum in the game" headline is partly a rubric artefact: the 15-axis set has damage_direct and damage_scaling for damage you deal yourself and only a catch-all "buff" for damage you cause SOMEONE ELSE to deal. deity/Knowledge does the identical through-ally amplification and scores 5/5 because it also holds a sword; Sovereignty scores 0/3 for the same function. Sovereignty is the purest through-ally amplifier in the game and is therefore the worst-case input to that rubric.
Second, the "White 3+ buys literally nothing" claim is REFUTED. data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json contains one @skills.white.rank, in handler SovFavorThp00000, formula (@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2) — Sovereign's Favor's temporary HP is a [Tier][Die on White], so White 3+ turns that grant from 1d6 into 2d8. It is a near-dead gate, not a pure toll booth (that title belongs to deity/Fate's White 2+, which has zero references of any kind). The real finding is card-blindness: EVERY Sovereignty card says "[Tier][Die]" and names no colour, so a player weighing a third rank of Black against a third of White is choosing blind about the only thing White does for them.

SO MY POSITION, in three parts.
1. BUILD THE DECREE, but only where the redundancy already is. Convert Sovereign's Balance (depth 2) and the Sovereignty capstone from single-target ally/enemy pairs into a Decree zone — a [Size]-radius area, scene duration, ONE active; allies inside Exalted, enemies inside Censured; capstone at +/-2 plus the reaction lock. That turns the tree's two most repetitive nodes into the two that keep the promise, gives it the only dual-polarity aura in 365, and needs no new talents.
2. MAKE THE ENTRIES PERCEPTIBLE, because a die step alone is not a turn-one fantasy and deity revision Principle 1 demands one from BOTH entries. Censure additionally prevents the target's damage die from being INCREASED while Censured — a genuinely unique counter to Knowledge's Insight multiplier, Power's riders and rival Exalts. Exalt folds in the temporary HP that Sovereign's Favor currently sells separately, and Sovereign's Favor is re-spent as the tree's Special (apply Exalt riding Draw Mana or riding the ally's Strike), which also gives the deity atlas its first Special.
3. PRINT THE COLOUR on every [Tier][Die] in the tree. This costs nothing and fixes the only defect a Sovereignty player is currently paying six skill ranks for without being told.
AND THE EXIT, stated so it is not left implicit: if the designer decides Verdannis IS a single-target arbiter and the zone was never wanted, then DELETE the Decree paragraph from data/path-descriptions.json and from the deity guide's Part 4. Parts 2 and 3 stand on their own either way. What must not survive this review is the current state, where the first thing a player reads about the god is a mechanic that has never existed.

CONFIDENCE: high on the diagnosis, every element of which is checkable in one grep. Medium on the zone as the remedy — the honest alternative is the deletion exit, and it is cheaper. NEEDS A RULING: this is a design-intent question about what Verdannis is, and it is precisely the kind of decision that EDHA_RULINGS.md exists to hold rather than a bench queue.
